newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Daimler says Jan-May car sales up 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Daimler says Jan-May car sales up 11 pct.

text.p: Sales of Daimler-Benz AG cars climbed 11 percent in the first five months of this year to more than 20.4 billion marks, Juergen Hubbert, the head of Daimler's car operations, said on Tuesday.

Speaking at a press conference to mark a test-drive event for Daimler's new A-Class model, Hubbert said unit car sales between January and May also climbed, but less strongly, by 4.7 percent to 275,100 cars.
Daimler distributed a summary of Hubbert's remarks to the media in Germany.

The car chief said demand for the A-class model, Daimler's first foray into compact cars, has been strong and the company sold the 28,000 models it plans to make this year in the first few days they were available.
The A-Class, which retails from 30,360 marks, hits showrooms in October.
Hubbert said Daimler was not running its A-Class plant at full capacity in order to ensure smooth production.
The company still plans, however, to produce 180,000 A-Class cars in 1998.

Some auto analysts had feared that the A-Class would hurt Daimler's image as a luxury car maker and that the company would have a hard time making money from the car, but Hubert said the vehicle was a key part of Daimler's model range.
"The A-Class ... adds a positive contribution to increasing the value of the car operations of Daimler-Benz," he said.
Daimler plans to produce a total of 700,000 cars this year, up from 645,000 in 1996.
